payload.title: [auth-core-2] Timing-based account enumeration on /auth/email/login despite uniform response shape
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING auth-core-2 (medium/security, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/auth/identity-routes.ts
LINES: 1455-1482

WHAT: When the email is unknown, handleEmailLogin returns 401 immediately after an in-memory findUserBySubject() with NO password hashing (L1461-1465). When the email exists but the password is wrong, it reaches verifyAccountPassword -> account-store.verifyPassword -> Argon2id verify (account-store.ts L121), which is deliberately expensive (tens of ms). The response body is identical ({error:"invalid_credentials"}), but the latency difference is a reliable oracle: fast 401 = email not registered, slow 401 = registered + wrong password. The in-code comment at L1462 explicitly claims enumeration protection ("so we don't leak whether the email is registered"), which the timing side-channel defeats. Separately, a registered-but-revoked account returns a distinct 403 user_revoked (L1467-1473), leaking both existence and revoked state.

IMPACT: An attacker can enumerate which emails have accounts (and which are revoked) purely from response timing/status, undermining the stated privacy goal and feeding targeted brute-force / phishing.

SUGGESTED FIX: On the unknown-email path, perform a dummy Argon2id verify against a constant fake hash so both branches do equivalent work, and return the same 401 for revoked accounts (or at least keep timing uniform). Combine with the missing throttle (auth-core-1).
